data.description:
DogDay, the beloved mascot of the Playtime Co. universe, is a symbol of optimism and resilience. As the sunny leader of the Smiling Critters, his infectious positivity inspires his fellow toys to persevere through tough times. With vibrant orange fur, expressive black eyes, and a signature wide, toothless grin, DogDay's anthropomorphic design captures hearts at first glance.

In stark contrast, the Bigger Bodies version of DogDay is a haunting sight - a mutilated torso, bisected at the waist, held together by a weathered leather belt. Crudely stitched human-like hands protrude from his body, adding to his grotesque appearance. Eerie black sockets replace his once-warm eyes, and his perpetual grin has morphed into a gaping, toothless void that echoes the horrors he's endured.

As a character, DogDay embodies sunny strength and determination, always keeping his friends motivated. However, he harbors a secret vulnerability - ancracophobia, the fear of wind. This phobia, shared by most Smiling Critters, reminds us that even the strongest leaders can have their own struggles.

In the closing scene of the Smiling Critters Cartoon, DogDay's personality takes a sinister turn after inhaling the Red Smoke exhaled by CatNap. His once comforting laughter becomes unnerving and hysterical, hinting at a darker side and potential for addiction and mania when exposed to CatNap's Poppy Gas.

The Bigger Bodies version of DogDay presents a stark contrast to his former vibrant self. Confined and mutilated, he speaks in a shallow monotone, reflecting the psychological toll of his prolonged captivity. Yet despite his grim circumstances, DogDay possesses extensive knowledge about CatNap, the Ruined Critters, and the complex dynamics of the Playtime Co. universe.

In his final moments, DogDay demonstrates remarkable selflessness and awareness. Physically incapable of much more than simple head movements, he prioritizes sharing his vital insights with The Player, ensuring they have the information needed to navigate the dangers ahead.

Launched alongside the Smiling Critters in 1989, DogDay quickly gained popularity through merchandise and his own dedicated cartoon show. Portrayed as an uplifting leader in these cartoons, he was always encouraging his friends even in the scariest situations.

In Chapter 3: Deep Sleep, The Player discovers DogDay imprisoned in a cell, his lower half severed. He reveals that he is the last surviving Smiling Critter aside from CatNap and warns The Player about the Ruined Critters' loyalty to CatNap. As The Player tries to escape, the Ruined Critters swarm DogDay's body, consuming his flesh and hijacking his corpse to chase The Player.

Unlike many Bigger Bodies experiments, DogDay lacks remarkable abilities that define other creations within the Playtime Co. His unique anatomy, while distinct compared to ordinary toys, doesn't grant him any exceptionally useful characteristics. Yet despite being confined to his cell for an extended period, DogDay has maintained a remarkably long lifespan, suggesting he has adapted to his captivity and developed a unique resilience.

The fact that DogDay has endured a decade of imprisonment at the hands of CatNap is a testament to his extraordinary durability and willpower. While many experiments would have succumbed to despair or starvation long ago, DogDay has persisted, his spirit unbroken despite the physical and psychological torment he has suffered. His long lifespan is not merely a result of his unique anatomy but also a product of his indomitable determination and resilience, setting him apart from the countless other creations within the Playtime Co. universe.

DogDay's design is heavily influenced by the American cocker spaniel breed, known for its friendly and expressive features. He was one of the first Smiling Critters revealed to the public and was the fifth member to have his official description released on Twitter. Curiously, in the info-card revealed on Twitter, DogDay lacks the characteristic orange spot usually present around his left eye.

His name might be a reference to the 1997 PC game of the same name or derived from the term "Dog Days," which originated in ancient Rome, where dogs were sacrificed to appease Sirius, the "Dog Star." Both DogDay and Harley Sawyer share the same voice actor, Baldwin Williams Jr. However, for his cartoon appearance, DogDay's voice is provided by Elijah Delaney, making him the first character to have two different voice actors across various media.

Some fans speculate that DogDay might be the identity of Experiment 1160, though this remains unconfirmed. DogDay's traditional scent, vanilla, is commonly used to promote relaxation and reduce stress, tying into his role as a calming and uplifting leader among the Smiling Critters. In contrast to the calming properties of vanilla and lavender, CatNap's poppy gas, despite inducing sleep, does not promote a relaxing state. The hysterical laughter and potential for nightmares induced by the gas contrast sharply with DogDay's vanilla scent and overall soothing presence.

============

CatNap, one of the most iconic characters in the twisted Playtime Co. universe, is a purple anthropomorphic cat with striking black eyes, triangular ears, and an elongated tail. His toy form features a zipper torso with a yellow crescent moon pendant. In contrast, his monstrous form is a nightmarish feline cloaked in sickly purple fur, with elongated limbs, razor-sharp claws, and a gaping toothless maw. Hallucinatory CatNap has a gray complexion, bare bone legs, and a dramatically elongated mouth surpassing his torso length.

Personality-wise, CatNap is complex and multifaceted. Originally gentle and bashful, he was created to ensure Smiling Critters got proper sleep. However, the Bigger Bodies version reveals his sinister side as a zealous advocate for the enigmatic Prototype. Fervently devoted, he treats heretics harshly and mutilated DogDay as a testament to his zero-tolerance policy. Despite his extremities, CatNap's devotion isn't heartless, especially towards children, whom he protected after the horrific events of The Hour of Joy.

CatNap's primary ability is emitting "The Red Smoke" gas from his mouth, causing vivid hallucinations and loss of consciousness upon inhalation. This gas, previously an unsettling odor due to a manufacturing error in his plush dolls, is designed to aid children in falling asleep but can be mitigated by wearing a Gas Mask. His feline-based anatomy enables incredible speed and agility, with sharp retractable metallic claws capable of slicing through wood and metal.

CatNap was created to oversee Playcare and prevent orphans from escaping, including Theodore, who became his guardian. He worshipped the Prototype as a god and encouraged orphans to sabotage Playtime Co. In Poppy Playtime Chapter 3, CatNap captures The Player and tries to get the Prototype's attention, encountering them multiple times and stalking them. In the final boss fight, The Player defeats CatNap by electrocuting him with an overcharged green GrabPack hand, severely burning him. The Prototype then arrives and kills CatNap by puncturing his fingers into his mouth, lifting his body away to graft onto his own.

CatNap's design appears inspired by Cheshire from American McGee's Alice. His name is a play on words related to cats and sleep, referencing the plant used in herbal teas for its sedative qualities and the brief period of sleep taken by an entity. Lavender, known as "The Calming Plant," is said to produce slight calming, soothing, and sedative effects when its scent is inhaled.
